Reporting directly to the Assistant Dean for Career Development, the Employer Relations & Recruitment Manager serves as the primary liaison to legal employers, maintaining relationships with potential employers to establish contacts to meet the career needs of UCI Law students.

Conceptualizes, develops, and implements programs, events, and communication strategies designed to serve employer and student needs. Continually develops innovative and effective ways to engage with employers to ensure delivery of highly customized and responsive employment programs. Engages in on-going assessments of the efficacy of current programs and services offered and proposes and implements appropriate modifications and changes. Analyzes employment trends, hiring data, and the needs and priorities of UCI Law students to make recommendations for changes to recruiting strategies.

Creates opportunities for employers to contact and recruit UCI Law students and advises employers on most effective way to convey their marketing messages to students. Works with employers to develop and facilitate long-term outreach strategies and maximize recruiting potential. Markets the talents and skills of UCI Law students to potential employers.

Manages all aspects of two large interview programs, including registration, scheduling and facilitating virtual and on-campus interviews. Maintains job opportunities database. Oversees system configuration, job postings, employer records, recruitment workflows, data integrity, reporting, and technical troubleshooting to employers and students to support recruiting operations.

Performs independently to identify opportunities to improve recruiting operations and develops, implements, and standardizes procedures to increase efficiency, streamline workflows, and enhance the experience of employers, students, and internal stakeholders.

Tracks and analyzes employer engagement, recruitment activity, interview participation, and program outcomes. Develops reports and utilizes data to evaluate program effectiveness, identify trends, and inform future recruiting strategies.
Ability to design and modify computer applications to meet program needs, problem identification, presentation skills, verbal communication, written communication, and organization skills.
Strong knowledge of career development theories, adult development theory, counseling process, career coaching techniques, career decision making, learning styles, and job search techniques.
Ability to work with people from diverse cultures.
Thorough knowledge of needs assessment theory, processes, and practice; workshop and program design.
Knowledge of UC programs, career services, employer, alumni, and faculty needs and expectations, recruiting and staffing methods, and employment trends.
